gloss: be ashamed, put to shame; come to nothing; shame
summary: To be ashamed: to be disappointed and disgraced when what one trusted fails, and to feel shame before others or before God. Those who trust idols, Egypt or their own strength are put to shame, while “none who wait for you shall be ashamed” (Psa 25:3; Isa 49:23); the penitent are ashamed of their ways (Jer 31:19; Ezr 9:6), and the shameless “did not know how to blush” (Jer 6:15). The noun בֹּשֶׁת is shame worn like a garment or on the face, and “the shame” is the prophets' name for Baal (Jer 11:13; Hos 9:10), put for בַּעַל in the names Ish-bosheth and Mephibosheth. The man and his wife were naked “and not ashamed” (Gen 2:25); Aramaic בְּהַת and Akkadian bâšu share the meaning.

words.gloss: be ashamed, put to shame; (hiphil) shame, act shamefully; (polel) delay
words.summary: About 120 times, nearly all in the prophets and Psalms: shame is what comes on a man when his trust proves empty or his wrong is exposed. Its constant companions are כָּלַם “be humiliated” and חָפֵר “be abashed”. The hiphil הֹבִישׁ is spelled like the hiphil of יָבֵשׁ “dry up”, and the brief files some of those here: Jol 1:12 (the joy that “withers”, a play on the withered vine of the same verse) and Jol 1:17 (the grain dried up) are יָבֵשׁ, and the qal at Hos 13:15, “his spring shall be dry (וְיֵבוֹשׁ), and his fountain shall be parched”, reads as “dry up” by its parallel. These are not given senses here. The polel “delay” is linked to the root only through the qal's phrase עַד־בּוֹשׁ “until shame”, of waiting or pressing until it became awkward (Jdg 3:25; 2Ki 2:17; 8:11); the link is not certain.

stems.gloss: be ashamed, be put to shame

senses.gloss: be put to shame, be disappointed
senses.definition: To be disgraced and confounded when what one trusted or hoped in fails: worshippers of idols, those who leaned on Egypt or Assyria, enemies whose plans come to nothing; and, denied, the hope of those who trust in Yahweh.

evidence.note: The caravans that hoped for water in the dry wadis: “they were ashamed (בֹּשׁוּ) because they had trusted; they came there and were confounded.”
“In you they trusted, and were not ashamed (וְלֹא־בוֹשׁוּ)”: trust kept is the opposite of shame.
“My God, in you I have trusted; let me not be ashamed (אַל־אֵבוֹשָׁה); let not my enemies exult over me.”
“None who wait for you shall be ashamed; they shall be ashamed who deal treacherously without cause.”
“You shall know that I am Yahweh: those who wait for me shall not be ashamed.”
“They are turned back, they are utterly ashamed (יֵבֹשׁוּ בֹשֶׁת), who trust in carved images.”
The makers of idols are nothing, their witnesses neither see nor know, “that they may be ashamed”.
“They shall be dismayed and ashamed of Cush their expectation and of Egypt their glory.”
“You shall be ashamed of Egypt too, as you were ashamed of Assyria.”
“Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel their trust (מִבְטָחָם).”
Ashamed of the oaks and gardens of idolatry.
“Let all who serve carved images be ashamed, who boast in idols.”
Servants sent for water find none and return with empty vessels: “they are ashamed and confounded, and cover their heads.”
“They have sown wheat and reaped thorns … they shall be ashamed of your harvests.”
“All who forsake you shall be ashamed … for they have forsaken the fountain of living waters, Yahweh.”
Jeremiah's pursuers “shall be greatly ashamed, for they have not prospered”.
“Let all my enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled; let them turn back, be ashamed suddenly.”
“The seers shall be ashamed and the diviners confounded … for there is no answer of God.”
“Nations shall see and be ashamed of all their might.”
“The moon shall be confounded and the sun ashamed, for Yahweh of hosts will reign in mount Zion.”
“Israel saved by Yahweh with an everlasting salvation: you shall not be ashamed or confounded to the ages of eternity.”
The servant: “I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed.”
“My servants shall rejoice, but you shall be ashamed.”
“My people shall never be ashamed.”
The man with a full quiver “shall not be ashamed when they speak with enemies in the gate”.
“Then I shall not be ashamed, when I look to all your commandments.”

senses.definition: To feel shame within oneself: the penitent ashamed of his ways, a man too ashamed to ask or to keep looking, and the shameless who no longer blush.

evidence.note: Ephraim: “after I was instructed I struck my thigh; I was ashamed (בֹּשְׁתִּי), and also confounded, because I bore the reproach of my youth.”
“My God, I am ashamed and confounded to lift my face to you, my God, for our iniquities have risen over our head.”
“Not for your sake do I act … be ashamed and confounded for your ways, house of Israel.”
“That you may remember and be ashamed, and never open your mouth again because of your shame, when I atone for you for all that you have done.”
“Were they ashamed when they did abomination? They were not at all ashamed, nor did they know how to blush (הַכְלִים).”
“I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers … for we had told the king, The hand of our God is on all who seek him for good.”
Eglon's servants “waited until shame (עַד־בּוֹשׁ)”, until it was embarrassing that the doors stayed shut.
The sons of the prophets urged Elisha “until shame”, until he was embarrassed to refuse.
Elisha fixed his gaze on Hazael “until shame”, and wept.
“Then you shall be ashamed and confounded for all your wickedness.”
“In that day you shall not be ashamed for all your deeds by which you transgressed against me.”

stems.gloss: put to shame; act shamefully; come to shame

senses.definition: To make another ashamed: God shames Israel's enemies and the counsel of the wicked, and the psalmist prays not to be put to shame in his hope.

evidence.note: “You saved us from our adversaries, and put to shame (הֱבִישׁוֹתָ) those who hate us.”
“You have put them to shame, for God has rejected them.”
“You would put to shame the counsel of the poor, but Yahweh is his refuge.”
“I cling to your testimonies; Yahweh, do not put me to shame.”
“Uphold me according to your word, that I may live, and do not put me to shame (אַל־תְּבִישֵׁנִי) in my hope.”

senses.definition: The participle מֵבִישׁ: one who brings shame on his parents or household, set against the servant or son who acts wisely (מַשְׂכִּיל) and the capable wife.

evidence.note: “He who gathers in summer is a son who acts wisely (מַשְׂכִּיל); he who sleeps in harvest is a son who brings shame (מֵבִישׁ).”
“A capable wife is the crown of her husband, but she who brings shame is like rottenness in his bones.”
“A servant who acts wisely shall rule over a son who brings shame.”
“A youth left to himself brings shame on his mother.”

senses.definition: Used without an object, as the qal: to be shamed when one's trust or hope fails.

evidence.note: “As a thief is ashamed (כְּבֹשֶׁת) when he is found, so the house of Israel is shamed (הֹבִישׁוּ), they, their kings, their princes, their priests and their prophets.”
“All come to shame over a people that cannot profit them … but a shame and a reproach”: Egypt's help.
“The wise are put to shame, dismayed and taken; they have rejected the word of Yahweh.”
“Every goldsmith is put to shame by his carved image, for his cast image is a lie.”
“Bel is put to shame, Merodach is dismayed; her idols are put to shame.”
“Moab is put to shame, for it is broken down.”
Ekron writhes “for her expectation (מֶבְּטָהּ) is put to shame”.
“Be ashamed, you farmers; wail, you vinedressers, for the harvest of the field has perished”, in a passage that plays on יָבֵשׁ “dry up” (Jol 1:10, 12).

senses.definition: To be late, to be long in coming. Its tie to “be ashamed” may be through the qal's “until shame” (waiting until it became awkward), but that is not certain.

evidence.note: “The people saw that Moses delayed (בֹשֵׁשׁ) to come down from the mountain.”
Sisera's mother: “Why is his chariot so long (בֹּשֵׁשׁ) in coming? Why do the hoofbeats of his chariots tarry (אֶחֱרוּ)?”

senses.definition: Of the man and his wife before sin: naked and not ashamed with one another.

evidence.note: “They were both naked, the man and his wife, and they were not ashamed (וְלֹא יִתְבֹּשָׁשׁוּ).”
After eating, “they knew that they were naked” and made coverings.
“I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid myself.”

evidence.locator: Isa.50.7, אֵבוֹשׁ → αἰσχυνθῶ; Isa.45.17, תֵבֹשׁוּ → αἰσχυνθήσονται; Isa.49.23; Ezk.36.32; Ezr.9.6; Gen.2.25, יִתְבֹּשָׁשׁוּ → ᾐσχύνοντο; αἰσχύνομαι renders בּוֹשׁ ×45

evidence.note: “According to my eager expectation and hope, that in nothing I shall be ashamed (αἰσχυνθήσομαι)”: the servant's “I know that I shall not be ashamed” (Isa 50:7).
“Abide in him, so that when he appears we may have confidence and not be ashamed (αἰσχυνθῶμεν) before him at his coming.”

greek.gloss: put to shame; (passive) be put to shame

evidence.locator: Psa.22.6, בוֹשׁוּ → κατῃσχύνθησαν; Psa.25.3, יֵבֹשׁוּ → καταισχυνθῶσιν; Psa.25.20, אֵבוֹשׁ → καταισχυνθείην; Isa.54.4 → κατῃσχύνθης

evidence.note: “Hope does not put to shame (οὐ καταισχύνει)”: the word of Psa 22:6 and 25:3, 20, those who trust and wait are not put to shame.
“God chose the foolish things of the world to put to shame the wise.”

parallels.note: Be humiliated, confounded: the commonest pair, “ashamed and confounded”.
Be turned back: the shame of a routed enemy.

opposites.note: Rejoice: Yahweh's servants rejoice while their enemies are ashamed.
Trust in Yahweh is what is not put to shame.
The son or servant who acts wisely, against the one who brings shame.

phrases.gloss: until shame, until it was embarrassing

words.summary: About thirty times as the common noun; the brief's count also takes in the names Ish-bosheth and Mephibosheth (2Sa 2–4; 9; 16; 19; 21), which spell the same word and have their own name entries.

senses.definition: The disgrace that covers the face or clothes a man like a garment when his trust fails or his sin is exposed; also the shame of the penitent.

evidence.note: “To you, Lord, belongs righteousness, but to us shame of face (בֹּשֶׁת הַפָּנִים) as at this day … because of their treachery.”
Sennacherib “returned with shame of face (בְּבֹשֶׁת פָּנִים) to his own land”.
“All day long my disgrace is before me, and the shame of my face has covered me.”
“His enemies I will clothe with shame, but on him his crown shall flourish.”
“Let them be clothed with shame and dishonour who magnify themselves against me.”
“The strength of Pharaoh shall become your shame (לְבֹשֶׁת), and the shelter in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.”
“Let us lie down in our shame, and let our confusion cover us, for we have sinned against Yahweh our God.”
“Is it I they provoke? Is it not themselves, to the shame of their own faces?”
“Why did I come out of the womb … that my days should be consumed in shame?”
“You know my reproach, my shame and my dishonour.”
“You shall forget the shame of your youth, and the reproach of your widowhood you shall remember no more.”
“Instead of your shame, double; … therefore in their land they shall possess double.”
“I will make them a praise and a name in all the earth where they had their shame.”
“Yahweh is righteous in her midst … but the unjust knows no shame.”
“You have devised shame for your house by cutting off many peoples.”
“They shall be utterly ashamed (יֵבֹשׁוּ בֹשֶׁת).”

senses.definition: The shame of the uncovered body.

evidence.note: Saul to Jonathan: “to your own shame, and to the shame of your mother's nakedness (לְבֹשֶׁת עֶרְוַת אִמֶּךָ).”
“Pass on, inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness and shame (עֶרְיָה־בֹשֶׁת).”

senses.definition: The idol, Baal, called “the shame” by the prophets; the same word stands for בַּעַל in the names of Saul's house (Ish-bosheth for Eshbaal, Mephibosheth for Merib-baal) and of Gideon (Jerubbesheth for Jerubbaal).

evidence.note: “You have set up altars to the shame (לַבֹּשֶׁת), altars to burn incense to Baal”: the two halves name the same god.
“They came to Baal-peor and consecrated themselves to the shame (לַבֹּשֶׁת), and became detestable like the thing they loved.”
“The shame has devoured the labour of our fathers from our youth, their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.”
“Who struck Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth (יְרֻבֶּשֶׁת)?”: Jerubbaal (Jdg 6:32; 9:1).
אִישׁ בֹּשֶׁת son of Saul, called אֶשְׁבַּעַל in 1Ch 8:33.

evidence.locator: 1Sa.20.30; Psa.132.18; Isa.54.4; Jer.3.25; Dan.9.7, בֹּשֶׁת → αἰσχύνη; αἰσχύνη renders בֹּשֶׁת ×22 and בּוּשָׁה ×4

evidence.note: “White garments to clothe yourself, that the shame (ἡ αἰσχύνη) of your nakedness may not appear”: the shame of 1Sa 20:30 and Mic 1:11.
Jesus “endured the cross, despising the shame”.
“Whose glory is in their shame.”

parallels.note: Baal, of whom “the shame” is the prophets' name.

opposites.note: The crown that flourishes on the anointed while his enemies are clothed with shame.

words.summary: Four times, always as a covering: shame covers the face or the whole man.

senses.definition: Shame that covers a man, for violence or for mocking Yahweh, or that God wraps round the king of David's line.

evidence.note: “For the violence done to your brother Jacob, shame shall cover you, and you shall be cut off for ever.”
“My enemy shall see, and shame shall cover her who said to me, Where is Yahweh your God?”
“Horror shall cover them, and shame shall be on every face, and baldness on all their heads.”
Of David's line: “You have cut short the days of his youth; you have covered him with shame.”

words.summary: Once, set beside the verb in the same verse; one use is a word scripture barely fixes, and its meaning rests on the verb beside it.

senses.definition: Shame received, the disgrace of Ephraim when its calf is carried off to Assyria.

evidence.note: “It shall be carried to Assyria as tribute to king Jareb; Ephraim shall receive shame (בָּשְׁנָה), and Israel shall be ashamed (וְיֵבוֹשׁ) of his own counsel.”

words.summary: Once, plural with suffix: the parts a man is ashamed to have uncovered, named from the shame of nakedness (1Sa 20:30).

senses.definition: A man's genitals, which a woman is not to seize even to rescue her husband.

evidence.note: “If men fight … and the wife of one … puts out her hand and seizes him by his private parts (בִּמְבֻשָׁיו), you shall cut off her hand.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܒܗܬ (bheṯ), with the Aramaic h for the Hebrew vowel: be ashamed, and in the aphel put to shame. It stands where the Greek has αἰσχύνομαι, ἐπαισχύνομαι and καταισχύνω.

senses.definition: To be ashamed of the gospel or of Christ, and to be put to shame or not before him at his coming; the Peshitta's word for the promise that whoever believes “shall not be ashamed”.

evidence.note: “Whoever is ashamed (דּנֵבֿהַתֿ) of me and of my words … the Son of man also will be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father.”
“I am not ashamed (לָא בָּהֵתֿ א_נָא) of the gospel.”
The steward: “to dig I am not able; to beg I am ashamed.”
“That we may not be ashamed before him at his coming.”
“That in nothing I shall be ashamed.”
“Whoever believes in him shall not be ashamed (לָא נֵבֿהַתֿ)”, after the Septuagint of Isa 28:16, whose Hebrew is לֹא יָחִישׁ “shall not make haste”.
“He is not ashamed to call them brothers.”
“What fruit had you then in the things of which you are now ashamed? For their end is death.”

senses.definition: To make ashamed: hope that does not shame the one who holds it, God's choice of the foolish to shame the wise.

evidence.note: “Hope does not put to shame (לָא מַבֿהֵתֿ), because the love of God is poured out in our hearts.”
“God chose the foolish of the world to put the wise to shame (דּנַבֿהֵתֿ).”
“Do you despise the church of God and put to shame those who have nothing?”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܒܗܬܬܐ (behttā), for αἰσχύνη and ἀσχημοσύνη.

senses.definition: Shame, above all the shame of nakedness, and the shame of the cross that Jesus despised.

evidence.note: “That the shame (בֵּהתּתָֿא) of your nakedness may not be seen.”
“Blessed is he who watches and keeps his garments, that he not walk naked and they see his shame.”
“He endured the cross and despised the shame.”
“Their glory is their shame.”

cognates.gloss: be(come) ashamed, come to shame; (D) put to shame
cognates.note: The same verb with the same sense, intransitive and causative, as the Hebrew qal and hiphil. Akkadian š stands for both older sounds, so it does not show which lies behind ש.

evidence.note: be(come) ashamed; be(come) put to shame; come to shame; put to shame

evidence.locator: atae x000041530, bâšu [come to shame] V
evidence.note: come to shame; put to shame (D forms ubaʾʾaš, lubaʾʾiš)

cognates.note: The noun of bâšu, formed like בֹּשֶׁת.

evidence.locator: armep x000066370, buštu [shame] N; armep x000060660, būštu [shame] N
evidence.note: shame; dignity

cognates.note: Oracc's glossary gives bāštu the senses “dignity, pride, vigour” and also “genitalia” and “shame”; if one word, its sense “genitalia” answers to מְבֻשִׁים. It may instead be a separate word (of bašû “exist”) merged with būštu in the glossary.

evidence.note: (a stone); (source of) pride; bearing; dignity; genitalia; pride; shame; vigour

cognates.note: Ugaritic keeps ṯ apart from š, and shows ṯ behind ש, as Aramaic t does.

evidence.note: Compare Ugaritic 𐎁𐎘 (bṯ /bâṯa/), Aramaic בְּהַת.

cognates.gloss: be confounded, abashed, ashamed; (pael) put to shame
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud: the Targum of Onkelos uses it in Gen 49:8, and “if I rise among the righteous, I may not be ashamed”. Aramaic t for older ṯ, with h in the middle where Hebrew has the long vowel; the Peshitta's ܒܗܬ is the same verb.

evidence.locator: s.v. בְּהַת, citing Targ. O. Gen. XLIX, 8; Y. Kil. IX, 32b (לא נבהת “I may not feel ashamed”); Y. Kidd. IV, 65c (בָּהֲתִין “they are ashamed of one another”); Lev. R. s. 31
evidence.note: “to be confounded, abashed, ashamed”

cognates.note: The noun of בְּהַת, which the Targums use for “shame” (Targ. Job 8:22; 2Ch 32:21) and which also means nakedness, as בֹּשֶׁת does beside עֶרְוָה (1Sa 20:30) and as מְבֻשִׁים names the private parts.

evidence.locator: s.v. בַּהֲתָא, citing Targ. Job VIII, 22; Targ. II Chr. XXXII, 21 (בֵּיהוּת); Ḥull. 56b
evidence.note: “shame, disgrace; nakedness (= h. עֶרְוָה)”

cognates.gloss: be confounded, perplexed, dumbfounded; (bahata) confound; calumniate
cognates.note: Close in sense to the Aramaic בְּהַת and in form to it, but Arabic t answers to Hebrew ת, not to ש from older ṯ (which Arabic writes ث); so it is not a regular cognate of the Hebrew, and may be borrowed from Aramaic or unrelated.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 263, art. بهت, بُهِتَ (n3385)
evidence.note: “He was, or became, confounded, perplexed, or amazed, and unable to see his right course.”

doctrine.statement: The fathers “trusted in you, and were not ashamed” (Psa 22:6), and the psalmist asks, “let me not be ashamed, for I take refuge in you”, because “none who wait for you shall be ashamed” (Psa 25:2–3, 20). The promise is fixed to a day: when kings bow to Zion, “you shall know that I am Yahweh: those who wait for me shall not be ashamed” (Isa 49:23); “Israel is saved by Yahweh with an everlasting salvation; you shall not be ashamed or confounded to the ages” (Isa 45:17); after the pouring out of the spirit, “my people shall never be ashamed” (Jol 2:26–27); “in that day you shall not be ashamed … I will make them a praise and a name in all the earth where they had their shame” (Zep 3:11, 19); “instead of your shame, double … in their land they shall possess double” (Isa 61:7). Paul takes the psalm's word, “hope does not put to shame” (Rom 5:5), and John sets the test at Christ's return, “that when he appears we may have confidence and not be ashamed before him at his coming” (1Jn 2:28), as Jesus said, “whoever is ashamed of me and of my words … of him the Son of man will be ashamed when he comes in the glory of his Father” (Mrk 8:38). From the verses: whether a man is put to shame or not is settled when Yahweh acts for his people, in Israel's restoration in their land and at the coming of Christ; till then those who trust wait in hope.

Those who trust in carved images “are turned back, utterly ashamed” (Isa 42:17); their makers are nothing and their witnesses “neither see nor know, that they may be ashamed” (Isa 44:9); “let all who serve carved images be ashamed” (Psa 97:7). The prophets name Baal himself “the shame”: “altars to the shame, altars to burn incense to Baal” (Jer 11:13); at Baal-peor Israel “consecrated themselves to the shame, and became detestable like the thing they loved” (Hos 9:10); “the shame has devoured the labour of our fathers … their sons and their daughters” (Jer 3:24). Trust in Egypt ends the same way: “the strength of Pharaoh shall become your shame” (Isa 30:3; Jer 2:36). From the verses: whatever is trusted in place of Yahweh, an idol or a nation's help, fails the one who trusts it, and its end is shame; Yahweh alone is “the hope of Israel”, and “all who forsake you shall be ashamed” (Jer 17:13).

The man and his wife “were both naked, and were not ashamed” (Gen 2:25); when they had eaten, “they knew that they were naked”, and the man hid “because I was naked” (Gen 3:7, 10). Shame came with sin, and the shameless are those who have sinned until they “did not know how to blush” (Jer 6:15; 8:12; Zep 3:5). Turning back brings shame of the right kind: Ephraim, “after I was instructed … I was ashamed, and also confounded, because I bore the reproach of my youth” (Jer 31:19); Ezra, “I am ashamed and confounded to lift my face to you” (Ezr 9:6); Daniel, “to you belongs righteousness, but to us shame of face” (Dan 9:7). Yahweh says Israel will be ashamed when he restores them, “not for your sake … be ashamed and confounded for your ways” (Ezk 36:32), “that you may remember and be ashamed … when I atone for you” (Ezk 16:63). Christ counsels white garments “that the shame of your nakedness may not appear” (Rev 3:18; 16:15). From the verses: shame is the conscience of sin before God; owned in repentance it goes with forgiveness, and the covering for it is given by God, not made by man.

The servant says, “I gave my back to the smiters … I did not hide my face from disgrace and spitting; but the Lord Yahweh helps me, therefore I have not been confounded; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed” (Isa 50:6–7). The gospels tell of Jesus spat on and struck (Mat 26:67; 27:30), and that “he set his face to go to Jerusalem” (Luk 9:51); Hebrews says he “endured the cross, despising the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God” (Heb 12:2). From the verses: the servant, a man helped by God, bore shame from men and was not put to shame by God, who raised and exalted him.

note: Brief: 172 tokens, 9 BDB keys. The zero-token cross-reference b.dl.ad (בָּשְׁנָה) is put with b.ax.ac, and m.ai.al, m.ai.ay (מְבֻשִׁים) with b.ax.ae, and b.dm.ab (בֹּשֶׁת) with b.ax.ad. Names: אִישׁ בֹּשֶׁת already has names/ish-bosheth (under ish, a.da.ac) and יְרֻבֶּשֶׁת is under names/jerubbaal (baal, t.cm.aj); both are left there. Mephibosheth (m.da.ay) is given names/mephibosheth here. The b.ax.ad count includes 2Sa tokens of the names (the brief shows the spelling בֹּשֶׁת marked also a.da.ac and m.da.ay). Hiphil הֹבִישׁ: the tokens at Jol 1:12 (ששון), Jol 1:17 and the qal at Hos 13:15 read as יָבֵשׁ “dry up” (no יבשׁ entry yet) and are given no sense here; Zec 9:5 “her expectation” is read as shame. Polel “delay” (Exo 32:1; Jdg 5:28): the link through עַד־בּוֹשׁ is a suggestion; no cognate checked (a lexicon's lead to Arabic bassa “drive gently” not followed).
